summary:
Flora Liu, an engineer on Notion's GTM engineering team, argues that GTM automation has shifted from a marketing ops problem to one of the more interesting distributed systems problems she has worked on. The starting state was a spiderweb: customer data scattered across Salesforce, Gong, Outreach and ZoomInfo, product usage in Snowflake, and years of critical context trapped in unstructured notes and meeting docs. Notion employees were already experimenting with MCPs and agents, but each department was innovating in single-player mode on a tiny slice of the journey.

The team reduced every workflow to four questions that became four architectural layers. Know produces a trusted context view per customer. Decide picks the single next best step. Act fires concrete actions such as lifecycle emails, in-app nudges, rep tasks, or reactive follow-ups parsed from Gong transcripts. Learn wires engagement history and lifecycle message performance back into the decision layer so the system self-heals, continuing, advancing, or pivoting threads. Humans and agents operate on the same loop: agents handle gathering, research, drafting, and summarization, while humans supply judgment, approval, and relationship ownership.

Implementation choices shaped the system. Agents never speak directly to customers; contact-sales forms are treated as untrusted input. Routing and eligibility became a first-class primitive, consolidating scattered rules to prevent double sends. The team chose to own the contact layer and rent the rest (email, enrichment like Clay, orchestration, CRM). Snowflake computes modeled entities, DynamoDB serves a denormalized key-addressable profile queryable in milliseconds, and the data lands in Notion where reps already work. Signals turn internal and external events into durable Temporal workflows, with retries, dedupes, and isolation ensuring one bad transcript cannot take down a batch. Every LLM step is traced for evaluation. A predictive engine drives lifecycle messaging when no signal is present, while reactive signals trigger grounded MEDDPICC follow-ups.

The shared Notion substrate lets new reps learn playbooks from encoded patterns of the strongest reps, raising the floor of the entire team. Build-versus-buy is decided per layer: rent what vendors do well, build where Notion's edge lies. Early results after 13 weeks show increased qualified opportunities for enterprise reps and 63% higher next-step likelihood for users receiving context-aware recommendations.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction: from marketing ops to distributed systems problem
sections.summary: Flora Liu introduces herself as an engineer on Notion's GTM engineering team and explains how building GTM systems has shifted from a marketing ops problem to one of the most interesting distributed systems problems she has worked on. A small team has been turning the stitched-together GTM spiderweb into a unified system.

sections.title: The fragmented GTM landscape
sections.summary: GTM solutions like lifecycle messaging, product recommendations, sales automation, and onboarding were historically fragmented because the underlying technology forced them to be. After a winter break spent building, the CEO returned convinced software engineering could tackle previously unsolvable problems, and agentic tech expanded what the team could execute. Liu argues customers experience one journey while internal systems support disconnected motions, forcing heavy context-switching on sales reps.

sections.title: Vision and initial challenges
sections.summary: The vision is a single programmable, proactive, and continuous decisioning system spanning self-serve growth and sales-assist. Challenges include no single source of truth across Salesforce, Gong, Outreach, ZoomInfo and Snowflake, departmental single-player mode innovation, data quality conflicts, vendor-introduced data latency, and crucially, unstructured notes containing signals like 'champion left' or 'blocked in legal' that automations must parse to avoid catastrophic errors.

sections.title: Four questions become four layers
sections.summary: The team reduced every workflow to four questions: what do we know, what should happen next, how do we execute safely, and did it work. These became four layers: Know (trusted context), Decide (single next best step), Act (concrete actions like emails, nudges, rep tasks, or reactive follow-ups), and Learn (feedback loop). Humans and agents operate on the same loop with agents handling repetitive scale work and humans providing judgment and relationship ownership.

sections.title: Key implementation choices
sections.summary: Agents are deliberately not allowed to talk directly to customers; humans approve agent work and contact-sales forms are treated as untrusted input. Routing and eligibility were consolidated into a single first-class primitive to prevent double sends and unify communication. The team chose to own the contact layer and rent everything else like email vendors and Clay for enrichment, since they understand customers best.

sections.title: Architecture: Snowflake, DynamoDB, and Notion
sections.summary: Snowflake computes the truth by ingesting vendor data and running transforms into modeled versioned entities (accounts, contacts, workspaces, eligibility, facts). DynamoDB serves a denormalized key-addressable profile queryable in milliseconds, persisting agent-generated artifacts like research snippets and rolling summaries. All this lands in Notion, letting GTM teams explore context, investigate accounts, and take actions like sending to Nooks or Outreach without tab-switching, while humans and agents share the same source of truth.

sections.title: Signals and the Temporal workflow engine
sections.summary: Signals are single customer events important enough to change the next step, including user-driven events like hitting an AI limit and external signals like funding rounds or tech-stack shifts. The signal service watches profiles, decides if an action is available, assigns ownership, and emits concrete tasks into rep Notion databases. The team shadowed best reps to encode sales workflows as durable multi-agent Temporal workflows, with retries, dedupes, and isolation ensuring one malformed transcript cannot take down the whole batch.

sections.title: Predictive engine and cold-outbound example
sections.summary: When no signal exists for a customer, a predictive engine recommends relevant product features and drives lifecycle emails, in-app nudges, and multi-channel communication toward adoption. Liu walks through a cold outbound signal example where a research sub-agent does concurrent research, drafts three emails, a scoring step ranks them, and a review agent selects the highest-scoring one, all orchestrated on Temporal.

sections.title: Reactive signals, Learn loop, and shared customer view
sections.summary: Reactive signals after a follow-up call parse the Gong transcript, extract critical MEDDPICC data (metrics, economic buyer, decision criteria, plan, champion), and draft a grounded follow-up; every LLM step is traced for evaluation. The Learn layer turns every action into a decision log and threads outcomes back to the deciding step so the system can continue, advance, or pivot. The shared customer and task views let reps start each day with a prioritized task box, pre-researched email drafts, and the patterns of the strongest reps encoded for new hires to learn.

sections.title: Build-vs-buy, results, and key takeaways
sections.summary: Build-versus-buy is decided per layer: Notion rents email, CRM, and orchestration from vendors that do them well, but refuses to outsource the context layer where its edge lies, since generic tools cannot capture its esoteric data models. Notion is built on plain markdown, an agent-fluent language, letting engineers, agents, and GTM work off the same context. After 13 weeks, enterprise reps have more qualified opportunities and context-aware users are 63% more likely to take the next step. Key takeaways include shadowing best humans before building, starting with the most legible workflow, modeling GTM as primitives (entities, context, triggers, actions, eligibility), and being headless by default so humans and agents read from the same substrate.

limitations: Each department was innovating in single-player mode, making holistic automation hard.
Data quality issues like wrong contacts tied to accounts could lose rep trust instantly.
Data latency from multiple vendors caused automation on stale information.
Unstructured notes containing critical signals (e.g., champion left, do-not-contact) could cause catastrophically wrong actions if not parsed.
It is very early; the system is still being built out with more features planned.
quantitativeClaims: In the last 13 weeks, enterprise reps have increased qualified opportunities.
Users who received context-aware recommendations were 63% more likely to take the next step.

evidence.excerpt: The most important facts about a customer were left in notes like the champion just left or don't contact this customer again. Um or they're blocked illegal.
evidence.supports: Motivating example for why unstructured notes must be parsed by automations.

evidence.excerpt: Every workflow could be reduced to four questions. What do we know about the customer? What should happen next? How do we execute that safely? And did it work? That became our architecture.
we designed our architecture so that the agent can operate as another operator within the same system as humans.
evidence.supports: Humans and agents share the same loop, not an AI layer bolted on top.

evidence.excerpt: we deliberately chose not to let an agent talk directly to a customer. For sales assist workflows, humans stay in the loop by default and approve anything the agents do.

evidence.excerpt: If a prospect fills out a contact sales form online, we treat that as untrusted user input.

evidence.excerpt: Snowflake, which is our data warehouse, is where we compute this truth. We ingest data from all the vendors in our GTM stack to Snowflake.
